# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**My picks**

| Need | Pick | Price seen | Key specs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall | Bose Ultra Open Earbuds | $199 (list $299) | 7 hr (19.5 with case), IPX4, physical buttons |
| Best bone conduction | Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 | $180 list, $125 at some retailers | 12 hr, IP55, neckband |
| Best for long or wet runs | Shokz OpenDots 2 | $200 | 10 hr (40 with case), IP57 |
| Best value | Soundcore AeroFit 2 | $79.99 at Amazon per SoundGuys | 10 hr (42 with case), IP55 |
| Cheapest way to try the idea | JLab Flex Open | about $40 | 7 hr (21 with case) |

**Why these**
- **Bose Ultra Open:** Runner's World names it best overall, and WIRED praises its clear sound and per-bud buttons, which are easier to press mid-stride than touch controls. Runner's World says it aims sound at the ear canal, so there's less leakage. The downsides are the price and the IPX4 rating, which is weak for heavy rain. Runner's World also says Bose plans a new open-ear pair within a month, so you may want to wait or watch for discounts on this one. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2:** It's the best choice if hearing traffic is your top priority. WIRED calls it the best option for bass and power while staying aware. Its drawbacks are that the band can clash with long hair and winter hats, and clarity is a bit behind the Bose. ([WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946))
- **Shokz OpenDots 2:** WIRED's top overall pick, and the reviewer wore them in the rain and fully submerged them without problems. Runner's World likes them for marathon-length runs. They're pricey, and Runner's World says the volume could be better. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** SoundGuys picked it as best budget. It has a hook design and adjustable fit, which many runners find more secure than clips. Open-ear designs leak sound and have no noise isolation. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))
- **Nothing Ear (Open):** SoundGuys calls it the best open-ear pair overall and best for running. It has strong bass for this category, an IP54 rating, and was $99 at Amazon (list $149). ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/))
- **JLab Flex Open:** Runner's World's budget pick. It has less bass and detail, but it's a low-risk test of whether clip-ons suit you. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/))

**Where to buy**
- Soundcore AeroFit 2: [Buy at Soundcore's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. The page lists $129.99 with code AFSC20 taking $25.99 off, and says it tested the code on 2026-10-22. That's well above SoundGuys' $79.99 Amazon price, so compare before buying. The code isn't valid on items already on sale. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2))
- For the others, I only had review pages with retailer buttons (Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, REI, Bose), not direct product URLs. You can find them in the [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), the [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/), and the [SoundGuys guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/). Prices change, so check at checkout.

**Safety note:** Open-ear earbuds let in more ambient sound, but they don't guarantee safety. Keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you.

If you tell me your budget, whether you run in rain, and whether you use an iPhone or Android, I can narrow this to one pick.
